<section id="methodology" class="methodology"><div><div class="eyebrow">READING THIS MONITOR</div><h2>A fixed spending baseline.<br>A changing market picture.</h2></div><div class="method-details">
<details open><summary>MOD spending & the £50m threshold</summary><p>Source: <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/mod-trade-industry-and-contracts-2025">MOD trade, industry and contracts: 2025</a>, Table 4a, revised 12 March 2026. This monitor uses the published 2024/25 figures strictly above £50 million. The table itself includes £50m; the one row published at exactly £50m is excluded here. Values are rounded to £ millions, so the underlying unrounded threshold cannot be determined.</p><p>Payments include the MOD Core Department, UKHO and Dstl. Foreign Military Sales are excluded. Joint ventures are attributed to holding companies in proportion to ownership. This is direct spending, not the whole defence supply chain. The spending baseline does not change with the weekly market update.</p><p><a href="data/source/mod-tic-2025.ods">Download original MOD spreadsheet</a> · <a href="data/listings.csv">Download listing mappings</a></p><details><summary>Original Table 4a notes</summary><div id="source-notes"></div></details></details>
<details><summary>Share prices, currencies & coverage</summary><p>Daily historical data is fetched from <a href="https://finance.yahoo.com/">Yahoo Finance</a> at build time. Nothing requires a live API call from your browser. The last completed session is shown, in the listing’s own currency: GBp means pence sterling. Prices are not converted to GBP. Treemap colours and percentage moves always use adjusted closes; this is a provider-adjusted price measure, not a calculated investment total return.</p><p>Each performance window is measured from the last session on or before its calendar start to the latest available session. The 5Y view uses all available data within five years; shorter listing histories are labelled. Quoted coverage uses explicitly mapped direct company listings, one per holding company. Subsidiaries, private companies, state entities and ambiguous ownership structures are left unmapped rather than assigning a parent or portfolio-company price. Listing mappings require periodic manual review.</p><p>Individual quote dates and stale download warnings are shown. Failed requests retain the previous successful series when available. This monitor is informational and does not provide investment recommendations.</p></details>
<details><summary>How news is paired with price movements</summary><p>Company-name searches of <a href="https://news.google.com/">Google News RSS</a> retrieve headline metadata and links, filtered for shares, stocks, earnings or contracts. Matching is name-based and may include irrelevant stories; it is not exhaustive. We do not republish article bodies. Each story links to its publisher through Google News.</p><p>Publication timestamps are converted into the listing’s exchange timezone. A story before the normal exchange close is paired with that date’s session; stories after the close, on weekends or on holidays use the next observed session. The displayed move is that session’s adjusted close divided by the preceding session’s adjusted close, minus one. Historical early closes are not modelled. A before-open story’s session move includes the overnight gap; a during-session story’s move can include price changes preceding its publication.</p><p>Stories without a subsequent completed session are marked pending. News coverage is limited to the latest 30 results per quoted company across the top 50 · past 7 days, irrespective of the chosen chart horizon. Only in-window stories appear as markers. Selecting an older story expands the chart to show it. The pairing shows temporal proximity, never proof of cause or a trading signal.</p></details>
<details><summary>Codex news briefings & weekly price context</summary><p>The main news desk covers the 50 largest suppliers by published MOD payments, including private companies. Codex writes concise summaries from the latest seven days of saved headline evidence, with dated source links. News after the last market close can appear here; it is not used to explain a completed weekly return. Every briefing records the exact snapshot it summarises. A new snapshot hides an older briefing until Codex prepares its replacement.</p><p>Briefings cover only the seven-calendar-day window ending at the latest completed session in the snapshot. For each listing, the return uses the last close on or before the window’s start and the latest close within the window. The largest absolute daily adjusted move is reported separately. Stale or insufficient price histories are flagged. Companies without a directly mapped listing receive an explicit no-quote explanation.</p><p>A separate, date-bounded company-news search prevents the general 90-day feed from crowding out the relevant week. Only stories published after the baseline session’s normal close and no later than the final session’s normal close, with a mapped session inside the window, can support a briefing. Weekend news after the final close is excluded. Company-name checks, quote-page filters and headline deduplication reduce irrelevant and repeated results.</p><p>The separate weekly price context is generated using headline themes and linked reports. The Codex news desk above is editorial prose prepared during a scheduled Codex update. A “reported catalyst” means a headline explicitly connects a price move to an event; it does not establish causality for the computed weekly return. Other headlines supply news context only. No explanation is inferred from a lack of coverage, and market or sector contributions are not calculated. Sources are numbered in each briefing; news searches may still miss material or include weak matches.</p></details>
<details><summary>Updates & reproducibility</summary><p>Data refreshes and news summarisation run as a Codex task scheduled by the project owner. GitHub Actions only checks, builds and publishes saved data when the main branch changes or a build is requested manually; it does not schedule or download updates.</p><p>The repository stores the source spreadsheet, reviewed ticker mapping, latest snapshot, Codex briefing and build scripts. Failed downloads retain cached data with visible warnings. Snapshot and briefing dates show the actual coverage. <a href="https://github.com/defenceeconomist/stockmonitor">View the code and update history</a>.</p></details>
</div></section>
